rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories after Noah show that his people’s fate was part of God’s recurring pattern for those who deny messengers, not a coincidence; the generations are left unnamed.
rows.anchor: ما أصاب قوم نوح على تكذيبهم له لم يكن صدفة ولكنه سنة الله في المكذبين لرسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unnamed generation is most likely Thamud: the cry fits their destruction by thunderbolt, the prediction of morning regret fits its timing, and their ruins remained at al-Hijr.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن المراد به هنا ثمود لأنه الذي يناسبه قوله في آخر القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elite’s speech is coordinated with the preceding account instead of being introduced as a separate dialogue turn, unlike the usual reported-conversation pattern.
rows.anchor: عطفت حكاية قول قومه على حكاية قوله ولم يؤت بها مفصولة كما هو شأن حكاية المحاورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They address their own people to stop the messenger’s appeal influencing the public, judging that this intervention matters more than replying to the messenger.
rows.anchor: ما هنا كلامهم الموجه إلى خطاب قومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reply is delayed: after the messenger continued repeating his call, they turned to their people, so the speech takes waw rather than the immediate-response fa.
rows.anchor: لأن قولهم هذا كان متأخرا عن وقت مقالة رسولهم التي هي فاتحة دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger’s call is reported with explanatory أن after the sending, not with a direct قال quotation; this also helps explain the different connective form.
rows.anchor: كلام رسولهم لم يحك بصيغة القول بل حكي ب ( أن ) التفسيرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere the people of Hud and Salih answer their messengers directly with rejection and rebuke, as shown in the cited replies.
rows.anchor: حكى الله في آيات أخرى عن قوم هود وعن قوم صالح أنهم أجابوا دعوة رسولهم بالرد والزجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين كفروا is a second adjective of الملأ, parallel to the wording about Noah’s elite; it is delayed so the following coordinated descriptions can attach to it.
rows.anchor: نعت ثان ل { الملأ } فيكون على وزان قوله في قصة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لقاء means one person’s presence with another; here it means meeting God for reckoning, and its attachment to الآخرة means meeting in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: واللقاء : حضور أحد عند آخر . والمراد لقاء الله تعالى للحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإتراف is making people live in luxury, and ترف means abundant blessing; Ibn Ashur points back to its earlier treatment in al-Anbiyaʾ.
rows.anchor: والإتراف : جعلهم أصحاب ترف . والترف : النعمة الواسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of the Hereafter removes fear of postmortem accountability, while wealth breeds arrogance and attachment to ruling rather than following; these traits help explain their rejection.
rows.anchor: وفي هذين الوصفين إيماء إلى أنهما الباعث على تكذيبهم رسولهم لأن تكذيبهم بلقاء الآخرة ينفي عنهم توقع المؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him merely a human like them is a metonym for denying his prophetic claim: they state the supposed premise that humanity excludes messengership and intend that conclusion.
rows.anchor: كناية عن تكذيبه في دعوى الرسالة لتوهمهم أن البشرية تنافي أن يكون صاحبها رسولا

words: يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating and drinking what they do serve as evidence for his ordinary humanity; the object pronoun after تشربون is omitted because its equivalent appeared in the preceding relative clause.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يأكل مما تأكلون منه } في موقع التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām introduces an oath; إنكم إذا لخاسرون answers the oath, while the conditional answer is omitted and inferred from it. The conditional particle enters the oath answer because of their similarity.
rows.anchor: واللام في { ولئن أطعتم } موطئة للقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيعدكم is an astonished question that shifts their attack from his claim to be a messenger to the message he conveys.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في قوله { أيعدكم } للتعجب

words: أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًۭا أَنَّكُم مُّخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is that they will be brought out of their graves after death and bodily disintegration, alive with a complete human form for resurrection.
rows.anchor: مفعول { يعدكم } أي يعدكم إخراج مخرج إياكم

rows.speaker: الجرمي والمبرد
rows.claim: Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad allow the second أنكم to repeat the first after an intervening clause, adding emphasis to the improbably phrased promise.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل الجرمي والمبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible parsing makes the second أنكم the subject, with the إذا clause as its fronted predicate; that whole clause then predicates the first أنكم.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أنكم مخرجون } مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers treat death and reduction to dust and bones as states incompatible with life and restoration of the human body, which fuels their incredulity.
rows.anchor: وجعلوا موجب الاستبعاد هو حصول أحوال تنافي أنهم مبعوثون بحسب قصور عقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هيهات explains the preceding promise and is therefore a separate, uncoordinated sentence.
rows.anchor: وجملة { هيهات } بيان لجملة { يعدكم } فلذلك فصلت ولم تعطف

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read هيهات with final fatḥa; it denotes distance.
rows.anchor: وقرأها الجمهور بالفتح . وقرأها أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads هيهات with final kasra; the word denotes distance.
rows.anchor: وقرأها أبو جعفر بالكسر . وتدل على البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هيهات is commonly repeated twice, as here, and can be repeated three times; Ibn Ashur cites verses by Ḥumayd al-Arqaṭ and Jarīr for the usage.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما تستعمل مكررة مرتين كما في هذه الآية أو ثلاثا كما جاء في شعر لحميد الأرقط وجرير

rows.speaker: جمهور النحاة
rows.claim: Most grammarians classify هيهات as a past-tense noun verb meaning ‘it became distant’; what follows it is its subject.
rows.anchor: أهي فعل أم اسم ؛ فجمهور النحاة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj instead chose to treat هيهات as a noun meaning distance, a fixed verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي اختاره الزجاج في ( تفسيره )

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib reports that some critics called al-Zajjāj mistaken for treating هيهات as a noun, suspecting the lām in لما influenced him.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : وقال البعض : غلط الزجاج

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad classifies هيهات as an indeclinable adverb.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هيهات ظرف غير متصرف ، وهو قول المبرد

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī reports that Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī alternated between analyzing it as a noun standing for a verb and as an adverb, depending on what came to mind.
rows.anchor: ونسبه في ( لسان العرب ) إلى أبي علي الفارسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sentence can explain and argue for their dismissal of the promised resurrection; it is separated from the previous sentence because it supplies the reason.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون بيانا للاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun deliberately precedes its referent حياتنا, first leaving the topic vague and then clarifying it; the later noun functions as an explanatory apposition.
rows.anchor: وهذا من مواضع عود الضمير على ما بعده إذا كان ما بعده بيانا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هي is not the pronoun of the story: it is explained by a singular noun, not a clause, and the construction with لا النافية للجنس also rules out that reading.
rows.anchor: ولأنه في الآية مفسر بالمفرد لا بالجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الدنيا means the nearer, present life; the negation means there is no life after this one.
rows.anchor: والدنيا : مؤنث الأدنى ، أي القريبة بمعنى الحاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ‘we die and live’ can mean successive generations die and are born, or that some die and do not return while the living continue until they die.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { نحيا } : نولد ، أي يموت من يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw in this phrase does not imply chronological order between dying and living.
rows.anchor: والواو لا تفيد ترتيبا بين معطوفها والمعطوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of resurrection is coordinated with the preceding claim, whose restriction implies only immediate life and death; the nominal form strengthens the assertion.
rows.anchor: وأفاد صوغ الخبر في الجملة الاسمية تقوية مدلوله وتحقيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the messenger a liar follows their argument as its conclusion and makes explicit the denial already implied by their opening claim that he was merely human.
rows.anchor: فجاءت مستأنفة لأنها مستقلة على ما تقدمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun هو refers back to the demonstrative هذا in their earlier statement.
rows.anchor: وضمير { إن هو } عائد إلى اسم الإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description ‘a man who fabricated a lie’ restricts him to that attribute in an emphatic reversal: he is not, as he claims, sent by God.
rows.anchor: فهو من قصر الموصوف على الصفة قصر قلب إضافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: افتراء is fabrication: a lie for which the speaker has no plausible excuse; Ibn Ashur previously discussed the term in al-Maʾida.
rows.anchor: والافتراء : الاختلاق . وهو الكذب الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They explicitly disavow belief despite the preceding accusation already implying it, publicly signaling to ordinary listeners that they will not be taken in by his call.
rows.anchor: وإنما صرحوا بأنهم لا يؤمنون به مع دلالة نسبته إلى الكذب على أنهم لا يؤمنون به إعلانا بالتبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa suggests that the messenger’s prayer was answered promptly.
rows.anchor: تقتضي الفاء تعجيل إجابة دعوة رسولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking them is a metaphor for destroying them.
rows.anchor: والأخذ مستعار للإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry is the sound of a thunderbolt, which confirms or identifies the destroyed generation as Thamud.
rows.anchor: والصيحة : صوت الصاعقة ، وهذا يرجح أو يعين أن يكون هؤلاء القرن هم ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing destruction to the cry is a rational metaphor: the cry is the cause of destruction or accompanies its cause, the air tearing when the thunderbolt falls.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الأخذ إلى الصيحة مجاز عقلي لأن الصيحة سبب الأخذ أو مقارنة سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment: the destruction was just, not an assault, because their wrongdoing made them deserve it.
rows.anchor: والباء في { بالحق } للملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غثاء is what a flood carries, such as dry sticks and leaves.
rows.anchor: والغثاء : ما يحمله السيل من الأعواد اليابسة والورق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a concise state simile: like flood debris, they decayed and piled in one place, dying all together.
rows.anchor: والكلام على التشبيه البليغ للهيئة فهو تشبيه حالة بحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting their denial, the verse curses and demeans them and their likes; it is not a literal prayer, since they have already perished.
rows.anchor: وفرع على حكاية تكذيبهم دعاء عليهم وعلى أمثالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بعدا is an absolute object replacing its verb, like تبا and سحقا, meaning may God send him away and crush him.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { بعدا } على المفعولية المطلقة بدلا من فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opposite idiom لا تبعد means ‘do not be lost’; Malik ibn al-Rayb uses it in a verse about his burial.
rows.anchor: وعكس هذا المعنى قول العرب لا تبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are the unbelievers: they wronged themselves by associating partners with God and wronged Hud by accusing him of lying about God.
rows.anchor: واختير هذا الوصف هنا لأن هؤلاء ظلموا أنفسهم بالإشراك وظلموا هودا لأنه تعمد الكذب على الله إذ قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural is comprehensive, including the people destroyed, and makes the sentence a concluding summary.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { الظالمين } للاستغراق فشملهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām clarifies who is meant by the curse; it attaches to an omitted explanatory phrase, making the condemned group explicit.
rows.anchor: واللام في { للقوم الظالمين } للتبيين وهي مبينة للمقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The impossible condition follows the statement that most people dislike the truth, intensifying the rebuke: their whims would bring ruin to the world and its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: زيادة في التشنيع على أهوائهم فإنها مفضية إلى فساد العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here الحق is the truth just mentioned: what agrees with objective reality and the true nature of things.
rows.anchor: والحق هنا هو الحق المتقدم في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هوى is desire for what suits one’s purpose, especially appetites that are not simply part of human nature; ordinary hunger and thirst are not themselves whim.
rows.anchor: فسجل عليهم أنهم أهل هوى والهوى شهوة ومحبة لما يلائم غرض صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whim includes wanting what nature does not require, such as injustice and humiliating people, or pursuing natural appetites in corrupting ways, such as stolen food or illicit sex.
rows.anchor: ليست من الهوى وإنما الهوى شهوة ما لا تقتضيه الفطرة كشهوة الظلم وإهانة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the truth is a familiar metaphor for agreeing with it; the counterfactual means that reality itself matched what they desired.
rows.anchor: والاتباع : مجاز شائع في الموافقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Existential truths are fixed in reality, including God’s oneness, His having no child, and resurrection for recompense; their truth is their actual existence.
rows.anchor: مثل كون الإلاه واحدا ، وكونه لا يلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moral truths are settled in human conventions and the world’s order: burying girls is injustice, killing is aggression, and gambling takes wealth without right; reversing them would corrupt the world.
rows.anchor: مثل كون الوأد ظلما ، وكون القتل عدوانا ، وكون القمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those ‘in them’ means the people inhabiting the heavens and the earth.
rows.anchor: أي من في السماوات والأرض من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم transitions from the previous question about their supposed madness to a new question about what could motivate their rejection.
rows.anchor: للانتقال إلى استفهام آخر عن دواعي إعراضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied question is a denial: they cannot claim that stinginess about payment is why they reject the messenger, since he asks no payment; even if he had, he returned it.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام المقدر هنا إنكاري ، أي ما تسألهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical payment taunt echoes other verses denying that the messenger seeks wages, including two formulations presented sarcastically.
rows.anchor: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This question rules out any cause of rejection originating with the messenger; after earlier questions about their own motives, responsibility lies with them.
rows.anchor: فالاستفهام الذي في قوله { أم تسألهم خرجا } إنكاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خرج is a designated levy or gift imposed on persons or land, such as a tribute.
rows.anchor: والخرج : العطاء المعين على الذوات أو على الأرضين

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī distinguishes the terms: kharj is levied on persons, whereas kharāj is levied on land.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن الأعرابي : التفرقة بينهما بأن الخرج الإتاوة على الذوات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported distinction makes kharj a voluntary contribution and kharāj a payment owed.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخرج : ما تبرع به المعطي والخراج : ما لزمه أداؤه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s argument treats kharj as broader than kharāj; the transmitted wording that reverses this is corrected in al-Farāʾid as quoted by al-Tibi.
rows.anchor: ( الكشاف ) : والوجه أن الخرج أخص من الخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharj is broader than kharāj, as the longer form adds meaning; if the prophet asked people for a little payment, the Creator’s greater gift would still be better, so this distinction is preferable to assuming synonyms.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ينبغي التعويل عليه لأن الأصل في اللغة عدم الترادف

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read خرجا فخراج ربك خير.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير }

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads خرجا فخرج ربك.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر { خرجا فخرج ربك }

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read خراجا فخراج ربك.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف { أم تسألهم خراجا فخراج ربك خير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the words are synonyms, the majority reading varies the wording to avoid an awkward nearby repetition; this is especially apt compared with the three-word gap before أجري is repeated elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فتوجيهها على اعتبار ترادف الكلمتين أنها جرت على التفنن في الكلام تجنبا لإعادة اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the words differ in scope as al-Zamakhsharī argues, the majority reading combines verbal variation with an intensifying rhetorical effect.
rows.anchor: وأما على اعتبار الفرق الذي اختاره الزمخشري فتوجيهها باشتمالها على التفنن وعلى محسن المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings that repeat the same form suit synonymy through paired verbal symmetry; they do not fit al-Zamakhsharī’s distinction between the terms.
rows.anchor: فتوجيهها على طريقة الترادف أنهما وردتا على اختيار المتكلم في الاستعمال مع محسن المزاوجة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the verses exhaust their excuses: the messenger is known and unlikely to invent his claim, seeks no worldly wealth, calls to Islam, exposes their failure to reflect and blind inherited religion, and faces baseless charges of madness despite clear signs.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ألزمهم الله الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical praise of God as the best provider completes the point by affirming His abundant favor and reinforcing that His provision is better.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وهو خير الرازقين } معترضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is part of an omitted speech addressed to the condemned on that Day: they are asked whether God’s signs were recited to them.
rows.anchor: مقول قول محذوف ، أي يقال لهم يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are Qur’anic verses, as indicated by the verbs ‘recited to you’ and ‘you denied them’ in their ordinary senses.
rows.anchor: والآيات : آيات القرآن بقرينة قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تلاوة means reading or recitation; Ibn Ashur cites prior usage in al-Baqara and al-Anfal.
rows.anchor: والتلاوة : القراءة . وقد تقدم عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is reproachful and denies their excuse.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غلب is literally to overpower; here it means being overtaken by misery rather than happiness, with the object ‘happiness’ understood from the context.
rows.anchor: والغلب حقيقته : الاستيلاء والقهر . وأطلق هنا على التلبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of غلبت is omitted but supplied by شقوتنا: their misery overcame happiness; the following على phrase names what was overcome.
rows.anchor: لأن الشقوة تقابلها السعادة ، أي غلبت شقوتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition على after a form of ‘overcome’ marks what is overcome, as in the hadith phrase ‘the men have prevailed over us.’
rows.anchor: والمجرور ب ( على ) بعد مادة الغلب هو الشيء المتغالب عليه كما في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their freely choosing causes of misery over causes of happiness is pictured as a state of inner contest in which misery gained the upper hand; it became theirs as it dominated them.
rows.anchor: مثلت حالة اختيارهم لأسباب الشقوة بدل أسباب السعادة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read شقوتنا with kasra on the shīn and a still qāf.
rows.anchor: والشقوة بكسر الشين وسكون القاف في قراءة الجمهور

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read شقاوتنا with fatḥa on the shīn and an alif after the qāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف { شقاوتنا } بفتح الشين وبألف بعد القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding قوما depicts misguidance as a defining trait and part of their collective identity, as in other Qur’anic descriptions of peoples.
rows.anchor: وزيادة قوله { قوما } على أن الضلالة من شيمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They imagine that, if released from Hell, they would return to faith and righteous deeds, so they promise not to resume unbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: وهم ظنوا أنهم إن أخرجوا من النار رجعوا إلى الإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘return’ is omitted because context supplies it: they would return to unbelief and denial, the acts that brought them to Hell.
rows.anchor: إذ كان إلقاؤهم في النار لأجل الإشراك والتكذيب
